subject: Onboarding: NewCorp network & service identity orchestration
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@newcorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Onboarding: NewCorp network & service identity orchestration

Hi Elena —

Great to meet last week. Per our call, this thread will be our coordination lane for the access controls portion of the onboarding: SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, IP allowlist, and service-account patterns (short-lived vs. long-lived). High level goals:

- Get SSO via SAML federated to Redwood test tenant by Apr 26
- Validate SCIM user/group sync with a pilot group (50 users) by May 3
- Agree IP allowlist ranges and fallback VPN pattern for admin tools by Apr 29
- Map service accounts and least-privilege roles for CI/CD pipelines by May 6

Action items for this note: please confirm (A) primary IdP contact, (B) SCIM sample CSV (if you have internal mapping), and (C) IP ranges we should allow. I copied Monica (CS lead) and Jordan (implementation engineer) who will own runbook items.

Attachments: I saw a reference to SOC2 evidence in procurement — if you can share the SOC2 PDF we’ll link it to your account record.

Proposed 30m checkpoint: Thu Apr 18 11:00am PT — confirm?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Date: 2029-04-17T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: NewCorp network & service identity orchestration

Ben,

Thanks — confirmed for the brief on Thu 4/18 at 11am PT. Quick answers:

1) Primary IdP contact: Rajiv Singh (cc'd) — he manages our Okta tenant.
2) SCIM mapping: attaching a CSV export of our group/user attributes (this is a trimmed sample).
3) IP ranges: Our networking team allows outbound to Redwood from 35.88.12.0/22 and 34.76.0.0/16; we can open a temporary dev range if needed.

We attached the SOC2 snapshot for procurement use — note it is a redacted PDF.

Small ask for the call: can your implementation team propose the service-account model (ephemeral vs. pinned) with examples for our CI runner? We have legacy long-lived keys and want to avoid that.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Head of IT Ops, NewCorp
elena@newcorp.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@newcorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-18T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: NewCorp network & service identity orchestration

Elena / Rajiv —

Good sync earlier. Follow-up notes and a minimal runbook for the pilot:

1) SAML handshake
- Metadata exchange: please share Okta metadata XML (or IdP SSO URL + cert).
- Redwood will provide SP metadata and ACS URL.
- Test flow: 5 test users (internal pilot group) — expect 10-15m to complete once metadata is loaded.

2) SCIM pilot
- I reviewed your sample CSV. We recommend mapping: username -> userName, email -> emails[0].value, groups -> groups[].displayName.
- I attached a one-page mapping suggestion and a sample API call you can expect during sync.

3) IP allowlist and fallback plan
- Production ranges: add 35.88.12.0/22 and 34.76.0.0/16 to account allowlist.
- Admin access: we recommend a temporary VPN CIDR (10.250.4.0/24) for troubleshooting windows; ops can remove post-cutover.

4) Service accounts
- Proposed pattern: short-lived ephemeral tokens minted by the Redwood service-auth broker for CI jobs with a TTL of 12h.
- Long-lived pinned service accounts only for audit/backwards compatibility; we suggest two pinned accounts with rotation policy + KMS-backed secrets.
- I attached a spreadsheet mapping suggested roles and permissions against your CI pipelines.

Next steps (owners):
- Rajiv: share Okta metadata and confirm SAML cert (owner: Rajiv) — due 2029-04-19 EOD
- Elena: confirm IP allowlist for prod/dev (owner: Elena) — due 2029-04-19 EOD
- Monica: schedule SCIM pilot and share test user list (owner: Monica) — due 2029-04-22
- Jordan: prepare ephemeral service-account demo and provide example CLI tokens (owner: Jordan) — due 2029-04-25

Thanks — I will circulate an updated runbook after Rajiv sends metadata.

Jordan Blake
Implementation Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
[attachment stub: map_service-accounts.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@newcorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Onboarding: NewCorp network & service identity orchestration

On Fri, Apr 19, 2029 at 11:13 AM Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jordan wrote: I attached a spreadsheet mapping suggested roles...

Team —

Sharing the Okta metadata file and updated SCIM attribute mapping (pushed to the shared Drive link). We validated the IP ranges with networking; 35.88.12.0/22 is good for production, and we opened the temporary 10.250.4.0/24 for your troubleshooting window. I uploaded the SOC2 excerpt to procurement as well.

A couple of clarifications:
- SCIM: we sync on-demand (not polling) — will that impact Redwood's expected webhook-based flow?
- Service accounts: we strongly prefer ephemeral tokens. If you can demo the broker flow and a token refresh during the 4/25 demo that will be ideal.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Example-Deployment-Docs

Regards,
Rajiv Singh
Identity & Access Lead, NewCorp
rajiv.singh@newcorp.com
